title: Occurrence-space and uniform survival products agree
statement:
Let $T$ be an indexed surviving trace of $\text{steps}$ steps, so that $T$ assigns to each index $i \in \bbn$ a state $T_i$ and, for every $i < \text{steps}$, the passage from $T_i$ to $T_{i+1}$ is a surviving step. Then
\[
\prod_{i \,<\, \text{steps}} r(T_i) \;=\; \prod_{i \,<\, \text{steps}} p(T_i),
\]
where $r(T_i)$ denotes the occurrence-space survival ratio of $T_i$ (the number of surviving edge occurrences divided by the total number of edge occurrences) and $p(T_i)$ denotes its uniform one-step survival probability (the number of non-crossing edges divided by the total edge count).
hypotheses_covered: T is an indexed surviving trace of `steps` steps (a state at each natural index, with a surviving step between consecutive states below `steps`)
replaced:
For every indexed surviving trace, the product of occurrence-space survival ratios equals
the product of uniform survival probabilities.
